title: DS-CORE: Rust implementation language and native-library allow-list
summary: Adds two technology constraints: server engine and server-side tools are written in Rust; native C/C++ libraries may be linked only from an approved allow-list.
rationale: PO decisions 2026-10-05: Rust for storage, Raft, GQL engine, CLI and bulk importer (operator and non-Rust drivers excluded); FFI allowed for reviewed dependencies such as RocksDB and aws-lc.

data.title: Rust for server and server-side tools
data.statement: The system shall implement its server engine (storage, Raft replication, GQL engine) and server-side tools (CLI, bulk importer) in Rust.
data.rationale: PO decision: Rust for memory safety and performance. The Kubernetes operator and the non-Rust client drivers are out of scope of this constraint.

acceptance_criteria.text: All first-party source in the server, CLI and importer repositories is Rust, built with a pinned stable Rust toolchain and cargo; CI fails if first-party C, C++ or Go source is added there.
Each first-party `unsafe` block carries a SAFETY comment, and CI reports the count of unsafe blocks per release.

data.notes: Open: minimum supported Rust version (MSRV) policy.

data.title: Native-library allow-list
data.statement: The system shall link native C/C++ libraries into Rust server components only if each library is on an approved, version-pinned allow-list.
data.rationale: PO decision: FFI is permitted for proven dependencies (e.g. RocksDB for storage, aws-lc for FIPS-ready crypto), reviewed per dependency.

acceptance_criteria.text: A CI check (e.g. cargo-deny plus a build-script/linker audit) fails the build when a native library not on the allow-list, or at an unpinned version, is linked.
Each allow-list entry records owner, purpose, licence, pinned version and review date.

data.title: Rust implementation with reviewed native allow-list
data.context: Implementation language for DS-CORE; scope options were server only, server plus tools, or everything; FFI options were allow-list, pure Rust, or crypto-only.
data.decision: Server engine and server-side tools (storage, Raft, GQL engine, CLI, bulk importer) are written in Rust. The Kubernetes operator and non-Rust drivers are excluded. Native C/C++ libraries may be linked only from a version-pinned, reviewed allow-list (candidates: RocksDB, aws-lc).

impact_notes.stories: None exist yet; no story links change.
impact_notes.code: No components configured yet. When planning, register server, CLI and importer as Rust components (language: rust) so trace tags are scanned.
impact_notes.evals: Planning must add static evals: a CI language/source check, an unsafe-block report, and a cargo-deny/linker allow-list check.
risks: RocksDB and aws-lc via FFI bring C/C++ memory-safety and build-toolchain exposure into a Rust codebase; allow-list review must be maintained.
The Rust driver (REQ-0043) can share types with the server, but the other five drivers need separate maintenance.
